item.title: Stocks, oil slip ahead of US threat of economic war against Iran
item.description:
Oil prices eased after strong gains last week while stock markets mostly faltered on Monday as investors awaited details of a US plan to impose massive economic pressure on Iran to end the Middle East war.

Wednesday's earnings report from chip giant Nvidia and Thursday's opening of the annual gathering of central bankers in Jackson Hole were also adding to caution on stock markets.   

In New York, the Dow was trading higher at late-morning trading, but the wider S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq were lower.

item.title: Explainer-What are Iran's options to escalate further in face of US economic threats?
item.description:
LONDON, Aug 24 - U.S. threats to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" to force Iran to buckle to its demands after nearly six months of war have raised the prospect of a new round of escalation in the Gulf.

How could Iran respond to the economic pressure?

CAN IRAN STOP MORE OIL GETTING OUT OF THE MIDDLE EAST?

Mohsen Rezaei, the former Revolutionary Guards chief and secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, has already threatened to shut down oil exports — one of Tehran's main strategic approaches since the war began on February 28.

item.title: US Treasury to broaden scope of secondary sanctions on Iran, source says
item.description:
By David Lawder

WASHINGTON, Aug 24 (Reuters) - The U.S. Treasury Department is expected on Monday to broaden the scope of secondary sanctions it can impose on entities and countries that maintain business ties with Iran as the Trump administration seeks to increase economic pressure on Tehran, a source familiar with the plans told Reuters.

item.title: Trump claims Iran 'collapsing' as US threatens 'economic D-Day'
item.description:
US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was "collapsing" as Washington prepared to announce the details of a new economic pressure campaign that Tehran has derided as an admission of defeat.

Almost six months into their war, the two sides are locked in a stalemate, with peace talks stalled, Iran keeping the key Strait of Hormuz shut and Washington persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.

Under political pressure at home over the economic impacts of the conflict, Trump has pivoted away from military action to economic levers.

item.title: Tunisian hospital receives 19 bodies after migrant boat sinks
item.description:
By Tarek Amara

TUNIS, Aug 24 (Reuters) - A hospital in the southern Tunisian city of Ben Guerdane has received at least 19 bodies of migrants recovered from the sea over the past two days, the head of a migrant rights group said on Monday, following the sinking of a boat at the weekend.

The sinking of the migrant boat, which carried seven members of the same family, sparked a wave of grief and anger triggering violent protests in the city on Sunday night.

Protesters burned tyres and blocked roads, while police responded by firing tear gas to disperse the crowds.

item.title: China's Xi likely to visit India with big delegation for first time in seven years
item.description:
By Saurabh Sharma and Aftab Ahmed

NEW DELHI, Aug 24 (Reuters) - Chinese President Xi Jinping is likely to attend next month's BRICS summit in New Delhi with a large delegation, three sources said, in what would be his first visit in seven years and a fresh sign of a thaw between the rivals.

India is hosting the September 12 to 13 summit, where Xi's presence would be watched less for the BRICS agenda than for what it signals about Beijing and New Delhi's efforts to stabilise relations after deadly border clashes in 2020.

item.title: Wreck of ship sunk by Israeli military in Irgun clash found after 78 years
item.description: The wreck of the Irgun underground's Altalena ship, bombed by the Israeli military in 1948 and deliberately sunk in 1949, was located off Israel's coast at a depth of 1,650 feet.
